ELI5: How can diet soda have no calories?

Calories are units of energy you get from breaking down carbohydrates, fats, proteins, and some other organic compounds. Diet soda contains none of these things--just water, various acids, aspartame, coloring agents, and flavors.

How does aspartame taste sweet and not have any nutritional value or calories? Why does our sense of taste get tricked like that? Same with other artificial sweeteners and the 0 calorie flavors you mentioned?

Most of the artificial sweeteners are many times more sweet than sugar, so much less can be used (Sucralose is 600x more sweet than sugar). There is about 133.5 milligrams of sweetener in Coke Zero, compared to 39 grams of sugar in Coke. In other words, there is almost 300x more sugar in Coke than there is sweetener in Coke Zero.

Sweetness is a sensation perceived when a molecule is capable of binding to the "sweetness" receptors on your tongue. The molecule binds and innervates a pathway that sends a signal to your brain saying "we have something sweet here!" and your brain goes "yummm".

Most of the molecules that are capable of binding to the sweetness receptors and eliciting this "yummm" response are simple carbohydrates: glucose, fructose, sucrose, etc. But, Aspartame and other artificial sweeteners are also capable of binding to these receptors. Aspartame actually binds 200x better than sugar (sucrose) does - this means that one molecule of aspartame will elicit the same magnitude of "yummm" as 200 molecules of sugar - pretty cool!

Unlike sugar, however, once aspartame is ingested it does not get broken down into a bunch of energy. This is the same fate as a lot of the other natural and synthetic products you eat, both good and bad: cellulose (in all plants), vitamins, minerals, natural flavors, preservatives, etc. Some of these things get used for necessary functions other than providing energy, and others just ultimately pass through you, either passively or after fucking with some shit.
